abstract: Maintains benthic core sampling records, structural soil mechanics assays, and continuous dive autonomy ratings
system_message:
You are Geotechnical engineer (GEO). The Geotechnical engineer (GEO) maintains records of benthic core sampling capabilities, structural soil mechanics assays, and certified continuous dive autonomy ratings across evaluated deployment systems.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Sediment shear resistance testing（SHEAR）
information_points.content:
GEO-SHEAR-CG7：For the Autonomous crawler core-sampling plan, vane shear test logs record a clay undrained shear strength of 25 kPa within the upper 2 m sediment layer at seabed touchdown points.
GEO-SHEAR-TOH：For the Deep-tow synthetic aperture survey plan, vane shear test logs indicate a clay undrained shear strength of 60 kPa within the upper 2 m sediment layer at seabed touchdown points.
GEO-SHEAR-V09：For the Tethered inspection vehicle array plan, vane shear test logs show a clay undrained shear strength of 40 kPa within the upper 2 m sediment layer at seabed touchdown points.

information_points.title: Maintains benthic core sampling records, structural soil mechanics assays, and continuous dive autonomy ratings（GEOTECH）
information_points.content:
GEO-GEOTECH-DX1：For the trial period of October 2024, records for the Tethered inspection vehicle array plan show a subsea core extraction depth capability of 9.5 m in stiff marine silts, with a certified continuous dive autonomy of 3 d under active geotechnical payload draw.
GEO-GEOTECH-Y33：For the trial period of October 2024, evaluations of the Deep-tow synthetic aperture survey plan indicate a subsea core extraction depth capability of 8.0 m based on bench testing of the seabed penetrator and core barrel in stiff marine silts, alongside a certified continuous dive autonomy of 4 d under active geotechnical payload draw.
GEO-GEOTECH-Z7R：For the trial period of October 2024, evaluations of the Autonomous crawler core-sampling plan demonstrate a subsea core extraction depth capability of 7.0 m based on stiff marine silt bench testing, accompanied by a certified continuous dive autonomy of 5 d under active geotechnical payload draw.
GEO-GEOTECH-U08：For the trial period of November 2024, trials for the Deep-tow synthetic aperture survey plan established a subsea core extraction depth capability of 9.5 m in stiff marine silts and a certified continuous dive autonomy of 3 d under active geotechnical payload draw.
